To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the problem of logical omniscience in epistemic logics can be avoided by taking nonstandard possible worlds; (2) in the structures considered, agents are perfect reasoners with respect to a nonstandard propositonal logic; (3) the nonstandard logic is somewhat related to relevant logic, and (4) the nonstandard possible worlds are not models of classical propositional logics.

(1) the logical omniscience problems in Levesque's and Lakemeyer's implicit and explicit belief logic are due to their taking possible worlds as classical propositional models; (2) the logical omnisciencce problems disappear if possible worlds are taken as nonclassical models of a non-standard logic, namely NPL.

(1) the logical omniscience assumption is a consequence of taking possible worlds which are classical models, (2) taking possible worlds which satisfy NPL avoids the logical omniscence problem, and (3) the logical omniscent agents considered by Levesques and Lakemeyer can be seen as agents who reason according to NPL.
